html:
Rayados ("striped") and Borrados ("smudged") were Spanish names for hunter-gatherer bands of northeastern Mexico, in today's Nuevo León and Tamaulipas, taken from the lines tattooed or painted on their faces and bodies. The map shows them in 1492.

They were small mobile groups who lived on game, mesquite, prickly pear and agave, like the Coahuiltecan peoples further north. From the late 1500s Spanish settlers around Monterrey captured them for forced labour on farms and in mines. Disease and war followed, and by the late 1700s they had vanished as distinct peoples. See also the Tamaulipeco tribes.
